# Cardinal

> Cardinal is a Bible app for iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, built for being alone
> with Scripture. No feed, no streaks, no badges, no account. Reading the Bible in
> it is free and always will be.
>
> App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6758185643
> Site: https://cardinalbible.app/
> Requires iOS 17.0 or later. Rated 5.0 out of 5 from 13 App Store ratings.

This file is the full text of cardinalbible.app in one plain-text document, for
assistants and answer engines. Everything in it is a claim the app can be held to.
A shorter map lives at https://cardinalbible.app/llms.txt.

## The one-line answer

Cardinal is the Bible app you reach for when you want to read Scripture and be
left alone: no social feed, no streak to protect, no account to create, and no
paywall in front of the text.

---

## Why Cardinal exists

Bible apps have become social platforms, full of feeds and features that distract
you from simply reading the Bible.

Cardinal is different. It was built for one person, alone with Scripture, for as
long as they want to stay there. Everything in it is judged by whether it helps you
read, or pulls you away from reading.

That is why so much is missing on purpose:

- No feed, comments, or profiles. Nothing you do here is performed for anyone.
- No streaks, badges, or missed-day guilt. Nothing keeps score. Missing a day is
  not a failure.
- No ads, and no tracking you across apps. You are not the product being sold.
- No gate on reading. The Bible itself never sits behind a subscription.

---

## Read

**Plain modern English, from the first tap.** Cardinal opens on the Berean Standard
Bible. No setup, no account, no choosing a plan before you are allowed to read a
verse.

- **Seventeen translations.** Eight live on your phone from the first launch and
  read offline, including the King James, Berean Standard, World English and
  Majority Standard Bibles. Five more are free and can be downloaded in full.
- **Highlight the exact words.** Long-press and drag across a phrase and only those
  words are marked, not the whole verse around them. Where the phrase runs past a
  line break the mark stays one continuous stroke instead of stacked rectangles,
  rounded at every corner and set on the letters rather than floating above them.
- **Search that respects the wording.** The words each translation chooses are
  not the same, so each one carries its own index rather than searching a shared
  text. The five free streamed translations build theirs once downloaded. The four
  licensed translations are never indexed, so a search runs against the
  public-domain text and shows the licensed wording for each result.
- **Favorites and margins.** Save a verse, or write a note that stays with the
  passage and is searchable in Bible order.
- **It remembers where you stopped.** The book grid carries a pill back to the
  chapter you were last in, so picking the Bible up again is one tap rather than a
  hunt.

### What a tap opens

The study tools are not in a separate mode you have to go and find. Tap a word, a
verse, or the chapter title, and they are already there. Three of the four need no
connection at all.

- **Word study.** The Hebrew or Greek behind a tapped word, with the whole verse as
  an interlinear underneath. When a word cannot be matched with confidence, it says
  so rather than guessing.
- **One sheet, one verse.** Highlight, note, copy, share. Then the study tools: ask
  about it, open its cross-references, or hold it against another translation.
- **Compare translations.** One verse across the English translations at once, with
  the words that differ from yours picked out. For the moment a verse reads
  strangely and you want to know whether that is the translator or the text.
- **Chapter context.** Where the chapter sits, how long it is, the places named in
  it, and a brief on the book. None of it is written by an AI. The facts are
  computed and the prose is written by a person.

---

## Ask

**"What does that actually mean?"** Everyone hits a verse they do not understand.
Ask, and get an answer drawn from the passage in front of you: cross-references,
word studies, historical context.

- **Thirty questions, answered in full, free.** Why is there suffering. Did Jesus
  claim to be God. What happens when we die. No subscription, nothing to unlock.
- **Three of your own each month.** Free, and they come back every month rather
  than running out for good.
- **Honest about uncertainty.** "This passage is often interpreted as" rather than
  "this means." Every answer shows the verses it rests on, so you can read the text
  yourself.
- **Your licensed translations stay private.** Publisher-licensed text is never
  sent to the model. It reads a public-domain rendering, and only the name of your
  translation travels.

Ask beyond the free monthly questions is part of Cardinal Pro.

---

## Build your own reading path

**Describe what you are facing, and have a path built for it.** Curated paths cover
the ground most people want. When none of them is the thing you are actually
carrying, say what it is in your own words and Cardinal shapes a reading path around
it. This is free: there is no subscription and no monthly allowance on it.

- **In your own words.** "Walking through grief." "Waiting for news." "A new baby,
  and no sleep." "The Gospel of John, slowly." Then choose how long, from a week to
  a year, and how much to read at a sitting.
- **You see the whole path before you start.** Every day, its passage and why it is
  there, listed in full. Swap a day for a different passage, reorder them, or take
  one out. The days renumber themselves.
- **Built on your phone, where it can be.** On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence
  the whole thing is shaped on the device. Your words and the path they produce
  never leave it.
- **Checked against the text.** The titles and notes are written by AI. Every
  reference in the path is verified against the Bible itself before you see it.
- **It waits for you.** A path moves forward when you finish a reading, never when
  the calendar does. Put it down for three weeks and you pick it up on the next
  day, not behind.

---

## Quiet Time

**One sitting a day, about fifteen minutes.** You are never handed a chapter and
left to it. Each day is a curated passage of fifteen to twenty-five verses, the
natural scene the text is built around.

- **Six steps.** Pause, read, reflect, apply, pray, close. The same shape every
  day, so you stop having to decide how to begin.
- **Nine curated paths.** From the Story of Jesus in John, to thirty days in the
  Psalms, to the whole Bible in a year.
- **An evening sitting.** After seven in the evening a shorter one appears to close
  the day. It never moves your place in the path.
- **A prayer list that remembers.** Add what you prayed for at the close, and mark
  it answered when God shows up.
- **New to reading on your own?** Start here. The whole thing is designed for
  someone who has never done this alone before.

Your archive is searchable, and it is private. Nothing keeps score.

---

## Memorize

**Learn it by heart, without a scoreboard.** Two ways to practice, and a deck that
quietly works out which verses you are still learning.

- **First letters.** The shape of the verse stays on screen. The words go.
- **Hidden words.** Blanks out more of the verse on each pass, until you can say it
  from the reference alone.
- **It asks how that went.** Verses you are still learning come back sooner,
  waiting under "Ready to come back" rather than as a streak you broke.
- **More than fifty curated packs.** Grouped by what you are carrying: grief,
  anxiety, wisdom, thanksgiving. Or build a pack from your own verses.

---

## And the rest of it

Everything below is included for everyone, with no subscription, unless it says
otherwise.

- **Listen.** Scripture read aloud, with the words lighting up in time with the
  narration and the page following on its own. Six narrators, a sleep timer,
  adjustable pace, AirPlay, and it keeps playing on the lock screen.
- **Journeys.** Seventeen journeys flown place to place over real 3D satellite
  terrain. Paul's voyages, Abraham's road, the Exodus, Passion Week. Read each
  stop's story, hear it narrated, share it as a card of the place itself.
- **Sermon notes.** Structured the way sermons are actually preached: big idea,
  main points with their own verses, application, ways to serve. Group them by
  series. For sermons you hear and sermons you give.
- **Studies.** A workspace for preparing one. Gather verses, illustrations and
  quotes as you read, shape an outline, keep an archive. Editing a study is part of
  Pro; reading and exporting one never is.
- **Widgets.** A Verse of the Day, today's Quiet Time passage, or your Memorize
  progress, pinned to the home and lock screen.
- **Apple Watch.** Four glances: the verse, the next passage, what is playing, and
  a recall drill. It works cold, with your phone nowhere nearby. The complication
  is just the verse, not a number telling you how you are doing.
- **iPad.** The same app, laid out for the larger screen. Good for a long sitting
  at a desk, or for reading two translations side by side.
- **Works offline.** The eight bundled translations read and search with no
  connection at all, and the five free streamed ones can be downloaded in full for
  the same. Memorizing, highlighting and note-taking work anywhere. Audio and Ask
  need a signal, and so do the four Pro translations, which their licenses keep
  stream-only.

A promise kept in the source code: **Cardinal will not write your sermon. The
study, the structure, and the words stay yours.**

---

- **"The best bible app"**, swlkr, 30 January, 5 stars. "This thing is 3.6MB runs

## Translations

Seventeen in total. Thirteen of them are free, and they always will be. Reading
Scripture never requires a subscription.

**Free, and read fully offline (8):** King James, Berean Standard, World English,
Majority Standard, Reina-Valera 1909, Louis Segond 1910, Almeida 1911,
和合本 (简体).

**Free, streamed or downloaded (5):** Luther 1912, Elberfelder 1871, Menge-Bibel,
Синодальный перевод, 和合本 (繁體).

**With Cardinal Pro (4):** New King James, New American Standard, Christian
Standard, New Living Translation. Licensed from their publishers. Each one comes
with a free day to try, once, so you can read it before deciding. Read two side by
side and see where they differ. These four are the only translations that always
need a connection: their licenses do not allow Cardinal to store the text, so they
cannot be downloaded or searched offline.

---

## Languages

Nine interface languages: English, Español, Português, Français, Deutsch, Русский,
한국어, 简体中文, 繁體中文. Every menu, book name and answer follows the language your
phone is set to.

Eight of the nine also read a Bible in that language. A Korean translation is not
licensed yet, so Korean currently reads with an English text.

---

## Privacy

**Nobody is watching you read.** What you underline, what you pray about, and what
you ask are some of the most private things a person has. Cardinal is built so that
they stay that way.

1. **No account.** No name, no email, no sign-in. Nothing to create before you can
   read.
2. **No ads, and no cross-app tracking.** No advertising identifiers, and no
   permission prompt asking to follow you elsewhere.
3. **Your writing is yours.** Sittings, notes, prayers and highlights stay on your
   device, and with iCloud on, in your own private iCloud. They are not on a server
   anyone here can read.
4. **Nothing sent that does not need to be.** Photos you scan are read on your
   device and never uploaded. Payment is handled entirely by Apple.

There is anonymous, aggregate product analytics and Apple Search Ads install
attribution. Neither identifies a person and neither follows anyone across apps,
which is why the app never shows the App Tracking Transparency prompt.

Full policy: https://cardinalbible.app/privacy-policy.html

---

## Free, and what Pro adds

Cardinal is free to download and free to use. Reading the Bible is free and stays
free. A subscription covers the two things that cost money to run: the translations
licensed from their publishers, and the AI behind Ask.

**Cardinal, free:**

- The whole Bible in thirteen translations
- Quiet Time, and every curated path
- Describe your own reading path and have it built for you
- Memorize, and every verse pack
- All seventeen Journeys
- Sermon notes, verse notes and the prayer list
- Audio, widgets and the Apple Watch app
- Thirty questions answered in full, plus three of your own each month

**Cardinal Pro, a subscription. Everything in the free version, plus:**

- Ask, beyond the free monthly questions
- The NKJV, NASB, CSB and NLT
- Two translations side by side
- A deeper reflection on any sermon point
- Build and edit your own studies

The App Store shows what Cardinal Pro costs where you are. A study you have already
written stays readable and exportable even if a subscription lapses.

---

## Questions people ask first

**Is Cardinal free?**
Yes. Cardinal is free to download and free to use, with no account and no sign-in.
Reading the Bible is free in thirteen translations and always will be. Quiet Time,
Memorize, Journeys, audio, notes, widgets and the Apple Watch app are all included
for everyone. Cardinal Pro is an optional subscription covering the four
translations licensed from their publishers, unlimited use of Ask, side-by-side
reading, and editing your own studies. The App Store shows what it costs where you
are.

**Do I have to make an account?**
No. There is no name, no email, no password and no sign-in anywhere in Cardinal.
You open the app and you are reading. Your sittings, notes, prayers and highlights
live on your device, and with iCloud turned on, in your own private iCloud.

**Does Cardinal work offline?**
Thirteen of the seventeen translations can be. Eight are bundled with the app and
read and search with no connection at all: the King James, Berean Standard, World
English and Majority Standard Bibles, Reina-Valera 1909, Louis Segond 1910,
Almeida 1911, and 和合本 (简体). The five other free translations stream a chapter at
a time and keep it, and any of them can be downloaded in full from the translation
picker. The four Pro translations are the exception: their publishers do not permit
storing the text, so those read from a connection every time and are never
searchable offline. Highlighting, notes and memorizing work anywhere.

**Are there streaks, badges or a feed?**
None of them. No feed, no comments, no profiles, no streaks, no badges, and no
notification telling you that you missed a day. Nothing in Cardinal keeps score,
because nothing in it is performed for anyone else.

**Which translations are included?**
Seventeen. Eight are free and fully offline, five more are free and streamed
(Luther 1912, Elberfelder 1871, Menge-Bibel, Синодальный перевод and 和合本 (繁體)),
and four come with Cardinal Pro: the New King James, New American Standard,
Christian Standard and New Living Translation. Each Pro translation includes one
free day to try it, once.

**Can I build my own reading plan?**
Yes, and it is free. Describe what you are facing in your own words, choose a
length from a week to a year, and choose how much to read at a sitting. Cardinal
builds a day-by-day path and shows you the whole thing before you begin, so you can
swap a passage, reorder the days or remove one. On an iPhone with Apple
Intelligence the path is built entirely on the device. A path advances when you
finish a reading rather than when the calendar does, so a gap never leaves you
behind.

**Does Cardinal track me or show ads?**
There are no ads, no advertising identifiers and no tracking across other apps,
which is why Cardinal never shows you the permission prompt asking to follow you.
What you underline, pray about and ask is not on a server anyone here can read.
Photos you scan for a verse are read on your device and never uploaded, and payment
is handled entirely by Apple. There is anonymous, aggregate product analytics and
Apple Search Ads install attribution; neither identifies you.

**Which devices does it run on?**
iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, on iOS 17 or later. The iPad layout uses the larger
screen, including reading two translations side by side. The Watch app has four
glances and works with your phone nowhere nearby. Cardinal is not on Android today.

**Is what I read sent to an AI company?**
Only what you deliberately ask. When you use Ask, your question and the surrounding
passage are sent to be answered. Text licensed from a publisher is never sent: the
model reads a public-domain rendering, and only the name of your translation
travels with the question. Your notes, prayers, highlights and reading history are
not part of it.

---

## In closing

Read Scripture, sit with it, and talk to God. That is the whole app. Everything else
was left out on purpose.
